items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] What about someone like Sonny Criss who I think you worked with. [INTERVIEWEE] Oh, he was a great saxophone player.

ctx.x: I grant you that. But there are a lot of saxophone players who would have been great on their own had they not listened to Charlie Parker. They emulated him to the point where they were…everybody knows he was an addict…they emulated him to the point where I’ve heard them say, “Well, if it makes him play like that, it will make me play like that.” I think that’s absolutely just somebody that’s weak that says things like that, because a lot of would-be great saxophone players, had they not listened to Charlie…
What about someone like Sonny Criss who I think you worked with.
Oh, he was a great saxophone player.
